{{Short description|Formula for buckling loads in slender colums}}
The '''Perry–Robertson formula''' is a mathematical formula which is able to produce a good approximation of [[buckling]] loads in long slender [[columns]] or [[strut]]s, and is the basis for the buckling formulation adopted in [[EN 1993]].  
The formula in question can be expressed in the following form:

<math display="block">\sigma_m = \frac{1}{2} \left(f_y +\sigma_e\left(1+\theta\right) - \sqrt{ \left(f_y + \sigma_e\left(1+\theta\right)\right)^2 - 4f_y\sigma_e} \right) </math>

with 
<math>\theta = \frac{w_{o,1}c}{i^2} </math>

where:
* <math>\sigma_m</math> is the average longitudinal stress in the beam's cross section
* <math> f_y</math> is the material's elastic limit
* <math> \sigma_e</math> is the average tension measured in the cross section which correspond to the beam's Euler load
* <math> w_{o,1}</math> the amplitude of the initial geometrical imperfection
* <math> c</math> distance from the cross section's [[centroid]] to the section's most stressed fiber
* <math> i</math> the section's [[radius of gyration]]

Robertson then proposed that <math>\theta = 0.003\lambda</math>, where <math>\lambda</math> represents the beam's slenderness.
